Environment setup: env vars, Docker, CI integration
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Alex, AE on the Redwood team. Priya is our solutions engineer. Quick intro?
[00:12] Sofia Morales: Hi Alex, Sofia here, lead eng at Linden Finance. Ethan (CTO) and Noah (security) are here.
[00:18] Ethan Walker: Yeah thanks, appreciate the demo - we're evaluating for a payments fraud assistant, mostly inference at low latency.
[00:25] Alex Chen: Great, goal for today: run through SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, auth patterns, env setup, and show Console + Optimize so you can see latency/cost knobs. Priya will demo code samples.
[00:35] Priya Desai: Hi all, I'll share my screen in a sec. Just to set context - typical integration is two parts: SDK usage in your app + optional use of Redwood Console for routes, keys, and rollout. We'll show both.
[00:48] [00:50] Priya Desai: (screen) Okay opening the quickstart repo - we have /python-quickstart and /ts-quickstart. The Python one uses pip install redwood-inference (placeholder name), auth via REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. Example: client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']).
[01:10] Sofia Morales: Quick question - can we do service accounts instead of long-lived user keys?
[01:14] Priya Desai: Yep, we support service account tokens scoped to specific routes. You can mint them in the Console or via our REST API. Good for CI/CD.
[01:23] Ethan Walker: And for infra, we're on AWS with EKS; would you recommend the hosted API or Dedicated? Latency is pretty important.
[01:31] Alex Chen: For predictable low tail latency and throughput, Dedicated is common - you get reserved GPU pools. Hosted is fine for early evals. We can show cost tradeoffs.
[01:40] Priya Desai: Back to code - TypeScript quickstart uses the redwood-js SDK. Example snippet: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); then await client.chat.create({...}).
[01:55] [02:00] Priya Desai: We also handle streaming tokens in both SDKs; the TS example uses an EventSource/stream handler for partial tokens.
[02:10] Noah Kim: On security - do you support SAML-based SSO for Console and RBAC?
[02:14] Alex Chen: Yes SSO / SAML for the Console and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC lets you limit viewing vs deploy perms.
[02:22] Noah Kim: KMS? We need customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
[02:26] Priya Desai: We integrate with cloud KMS/HSMs - AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and support bring-your-own keys in Private deployments. For Hosted we also have envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping.
[02:40] [02:45] Sofia Morales: How about audit logs and retention - we need 12 months of request logs for compliance.
[02:50] Alex Chen: We offer audit log retention options (Console add-on). For Private deployments you keep logs in your VPC, and Dedicated has audit exports too. We'll send our SOC 2 & security whitepaper.
[03:05] Priya Desai: Alright I'm going to run the python quickstart live. Opening terminal. (typo) pip install redwood-inferance - oops that's a bad transcribe. Correct package name in repo.
[03:25] [03:30] Priya Desai: Create file quickstart.py - import os; from redwood import Redwood; client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']); resp = client.generate("Summarize payment dispute details for order id 12345"); print(resp.text)
[03:50] Ethan Walker: Nice, how do you recommend storing the API key in production?
[03:54] Priya Desai: Use secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager / Parameter Store), or set it as a CI/CD secret. For k8s we recommend sealed-secrets or K8s Secrets encrypted with KMS.
[04:08] Maya Li: Quick question on environment parity - any Docker sample?
[04:12] Priya Desai: Yes repo includes a Dockerfile and a docker-compose for local testing. Example sets ENV REDWOOD_API_KEY and runs the app.
[04:20] [04:30] Priya Desai: Now the TS sample - sample Next.js app with server-side route hitting Redwood. We emphasize server-side calls for security; client-side only for embeddings with short-lived tokens.
[04:45] Sofia Morales: Do you support short-lived ephemeral tokens for browser flows?
[04:48] Alex Chen: Yes, we issue ephemeral tokens scoped to an embedding or a particular route, lifetime configurable. Good for client-side embedding calls.
[05:00] Priya Desai: Moving to auth flows - three common patterns: 1) API key (server-to-server), 2) service accounts (CI/CD), 3) ephemeral tokens (client). The Console shows key rotation and scopes.
[05:18] Noah Kim: On telemetry and PII - we need assurances that user PII isn't retained. How does Redwood handle data retention?
[05:25] Alex Chen: We have retention policies and options to disable training on customer data. For Hosted we offer configurable retention windows; for Private and Dedicated you control full retention.
[05:38] [05:45] Priya Desai: Quick UX: Console -> Create Route -> Attach Model (we have curated open models + Redwood-verified profiles). We can pin model versions and rollout with canary policies.
[05:58] Ethan Walker: Are model variants like quantized versions available automatically? We need cost controls.
[06:03] Priya Desai: Yes Optimize gives recommendations - quantization profiles, batch sizes. You can run quality regressions tied to prompt sets. We recommend starting with int8 for background tasks, int4 on Dedicated for cost-sensitive runs after validation.
[06:20] [06:30] Priya Desai: For POC scope, what would success look like for you?
[06:35] Sofia Morales: Latency under 150ms p95 for single-turn inference, cost per 1k tokens under $0.XX (TBD), and no data retention in hosted or confirmation of deletes.
[06:46] Ethan Walker: We also want to see horizontal scaling behavior at 500 QPS.
[06:50] Alex Chen: Good - sounds like Dedicated POC. We'll propose a reserved pool with autoscaling and a benchmark plan.
[07:00] [07:05] Priya Desai: Now I'll demo a simple CI example: GitHub Actions job that runs unit tests and hits Redwood via service account. Steps: checkout, set REDWOOD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN secret, run pytest. We also provide Terraform snippets to create service accounts and route configs.
[07:24] Sofia Morales: Can we automate canary rollouts?
[07:27] Priya Desai: Yes, Console supports percentage-based rollouts and automatic fallback rules if error rate or latency crosses thresholds.
[07:36] [07:45] Noah Kim: About network controls - can we restrict access to specific VPC endpoints?
[07:49] Alex Chen: For Private deployments, yes. For Dedicated you can enable private networking and allowlist by VPC peering or PrivateLink equivalents.
[07:59] Priya Desai: I'm going to show how streaming looks in the TS quickstart - you get partial tokens to reduce time-to-first-byte. In Console you can enable streaming per-route.
[08:14] [08:20] (minor crosstalk)
[08:25] Priya Desai: Let's switch to troubleshooting section - common integration issues: 1) missing env var (API key), 2) wrong scopes on token, 3) hitting rate limits because route default is low - use per-route quotas in the Console.
[08:39] Sofia Morales: Do you expose per-route metrics? We need to attribute cost to product teams.
[08:43] Alex Chen: Yes, Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and trace hooks you can correlate with internal request IDs.
[08:53] [09:00] Ethan Walker: For CI load testing - any recommended toolchain?
[09:04] Priya Desai: Folks use vegeta or k6; we'll share a sample benchmark script that can replay production prompt sets with variable concurrency. That script respects batching and warm-up for KV cache.
[09:20] Noah Kim: On cryptography - do you support HSM-backed keys for signing or audit log tamper-proofing?
[09:27] Alex Chen: For Private you can integrate HSMs. For hosted we can provide additional attestation and log exports; we'll follow up with the security team.
[09:40] Priya Desai: Quick note about embeddings: use server-side calls with short-lived tokens if you're creating client-side embedding features. We also have vector store connectors in the repo for Pinecone/Weaviate etc.
[09:58] [10:05] Sofia Morales: All great - can you paste the quickstart link in chat?
[10:08] Alex Chen: Yes sending now (link to github.com/redwood/quickstarts).
[10:12] Priya Desai: I'm going to demo a small end-to-end: local dev -> Console route -> production route. Starting with local env, set REDWOOD_API_KEY; run app; check Console logs.
[10:25] [10:30] Priya Desai: Here in Console you can see a sample request - latency 78ms, tokens 120, cost $0.00x. The Console also highlights model mismatches if the model fails quality checks.
[10:44] Ethan Walker: Regarding billing - can we get consolidated invoices across orgs and per-route chargebacks?
[10:49] Alex Chen: Yes, Enterprise billing supports consolidated billing and cost allocation tags. We'll include billing docs.
[10:57] [11:05] Priya Desai: One more sample - toggling Optimize suggestions: it recommended increasing batch size to 8 and enabling prefix caching for repeated prompt patterns, estimated 25% cost reduction.
[11:20] Sofia Morales: How do you measure regressions when changing quantization?
[11:24] Priya Desai: We tie eval prompt sets to rollouts - when you change model profile or quantization, Redwood runs the evals and shows a quality delta. You can gate rollouts on regression thresholds.
[11:38] [11:45] Ethan Walker: For POC timeline, we aim to start in two weeks - can you commit to delivering sample infra and a benchmark plan before then?
[11:52] Alex Chen: Yes - we'll share the repo and a proposed benchmark plan by Friday.
[11:58] Priya Desai: I'll also include Terraform snippets to create routes and service accounts, plus CI examples.
[12:05] [12:12] Noah Kim: On data residency - our legal team requires EU-only processing for EU customers. Is that configurable?
[12:18] Alex Chen: Yes - routes can be pinned to region, and for Dedicated/Private you can ensure EU-only data paths. We'll document region controls.
[12:32] Sofia Morales: Any known limitations with long-context models? We have 16k token use cases for chat history.
[12:37] Priya Desai: We support longer context models; runtime chooses kernels and KV cache strategies. For long histories we recommend prefix caching and summarized context to reduce cost.
[12:50] [12:55] Alex Chen: Alright quick recap: we'll send quickstart repo, SDK examples, Terraform snippets, security docs (SOC2, KMS, audit logs), and a pricing + Dedicated POC proposal. We'll schedule a benchmark next Wednesday.
[13:12] Ethan Walker: Sounds good. Thanks Alex and Priya.
[13:16] Sofia Morales: Thanks everyone.
[13:20] Alex Chen: Thanks - I'll follow up with an email and the links.
[13:25] (call ends)

Notes: transcript includes minor transcription typos (package name, slight word swaps). Console and Optimize feature names used for clarity.
